hints: Recall the defining relation for a wire $R = \rho L/A$, where $R$ is in $\Omega$, $L$ in $\text{m}$ and $A$ in $\text{m}^2$.
Rearrange it to make resistivity the subject as $\rho = RA/L$ so you can see how the units combine.
Multiply the unit of $R$ by the unit of $A$ and then divide by the unit of $L$ to simplify to a single length power.
walkthrough: Start from the resistance of a uniform wire: $R = \rho L / A$, where $L$ is length and $A$ is cross-sectional area.
Rearrange for resistivity: $\rho = RA/L$, so resistivity depends on resistance times area divided by length.
Insert units: $R$ has unit $\Omega$, $A$ has unit $\text{m}^2$ and $L$ has unit $\text{m}$.

options.A: This would be resistance divided by area squared and does not follow from $\rho = RA/L$.
options.B: This is the unit of conductivity reciprocal length dependence, since conductivity has unit $\Omega^{-1} \text{m}^{-1}$.
options.C: This is the unit of resistance $R$, not of the material property resistivity $\rho$.
